title: controlplane-egress-lockdown-with-route53-resolver-integration
author: Priya Nair
description: Background: customer private control planes require strict egress policies but also need DNS resolution to Redwood control-plane endpoints and private model registries in cross-account deployments. This PR adds a least-privilege egress security group for control-plane subnets, provisions Route53 Resolver endpoints (outbound+inbound where requested) via Terraform modules, and wires resolver rules so private DNS for *.redwood.internal resolves to the vendor VPC resolver. It also updates the private-installer Helm chart to support configuring resolver endpoint IDs and exposes a safe rollout path with a dry-run mode. Summary of changes: 1) Terraform: new module redwood_vpc_dns_resolver that creates Route53 Resolver outbound endpoints, resolver rules, and conditional inbound endpoints (for on-prem VPN/Direct Connect scenarios); supports tagging, secondary-secondary-subnet placement for HA, and explicit security group attachment. 2) Security: new controlplane_egress_sg with explicit allow-list egress for: - Route53 Resolver IPs (port 53 UDP/TCP) - TLS egress to platform endpoints (443) to specific prefix-lists supplied by the control plane account - NTP (123/UDP) to customer-provided NTP CIDRs (configurable) All other egress is denied by default. 3) Helm: chart values.schema updated with resolver.enabled, resolver.outbound_endpoint_id, resolver.inbound_endpoint_id, resolver.rule_name, and installer.dryRun to support preflight validation without applying route changes. 4) Installer orchestration: adds a two-phase rollout; phase A creates outbound endpoint and resolver rules and attaches the egress SG in a permissive verification mode, phase B flips the SG to enforce deny-by-default and tears down permissive verification hooks. 5) Docs and upgrade: added upgrade notes and rollback steps for both Terraform and Helm paths and a script to back out resolver rules in 1 command. Motivation: several customers hit operational surprises when egress was wide-open and DNS leaked to public resolvers; this reduces blast radius while preserving resolution for platform-hosted edges. Testing and validation performed: - Unit/integration Terraform plan and apply in a dedicated test AWS account using the new module - Helm template rendering across supported chart versions and dry-run mode validation - End-to-end validation that control-plane pods can resolve and reach *.control.redwood.internal and model-registry.private.redwood.internal after outbound endpoints are provisioned - Failover test: simulated subnet failure by draining one AZ and ensuring resolver HA works - Security audit: manual review of SG rules to enforce least privilege and avoid 0.0.0.0/0 egress. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy module in staging with resolver.enabled=true and installer.dryRun=true 2) Verify DNS via the staging control plane and metrics for DNS latency/error 3) Flip dryRun to false and apply SG enforcement in a maintenance window 4) Monitor for 48 hours and use rollback script if anomalous resolution or app connectivity occurs. Rollback: instructions added to docs/installer/rollback-resolver.md and implemented as a terraform destroy target plus Helm values revert. Related: builds on ENG-4872 (subnet isolation work) and closes ENG-5127. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module implemented and unit-tested - [x] Helm values/schema updated - [x] E2E validation in staging account - [x] Security review completed - [x] Upgrade and rollback docs added - [x] CI passes (lint/terraform fmt/helm lint) See also: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5127/control-plane-egress-and-dns-resolver-design and internal runbook https://redwood-internal.example.com/runbooks/controlplane-dns-egress.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can we avoid creating inbound resolver endpoints by default? Suggest making inbound endpoints opt-in via variable resolver.create_inbound (response: PR author: made inbound endpoint opt-in with resolver.create_inbound default=false)
Marta Lopez: Needs a note about resolver rules priority and how they interact with existing customer rules (response: added rule_name and priority docs and validation)
Jun Park: Please add unit tests that assert the SG does not contain 0.0.0.0/0 egress after apply (response: added terraform test and manual audit note)
Security Bot (automated scan): flagged potential NTP wide-open rule in initial patch (response: restricted NTP to customer NTP CIDR and documented requirement)
release_notes: Private-installer: adds Route53 Resolver integration for private control planes; introduces controlplane_egress_sg to enforce least-privilege egress; Helm chart knobs for resolver endpoints and a dryRun installer mode.
Upgrade notes: follow installer/upgrade/rollback-resolver.md for staged rollout; default behavior is no inbound endpoints to avoid unexpected inbound DNS exposure.
